title: Red Jellyfish
place: Hydrographer Canyon water column, ~700 m, off New England, North Atlantic (EX2104 Dive 20)
audio: none (the source track was digital silence, so it was removed)
notes: The only CREATURE scene, an eerie highlight. A large blood-red, pillow-shaped jellyfish (genus Poralia, possibly an undescribed species) drifts in blue darkness with marine snow. 0-2.5 s: a pinkish bell, upper-left of centre (x~0.35), with a thin white streak (a small drifting animal or particle) crossing it. 2.5-14 s: the bell turns deep red and glowing as the ROV lights hit it, slowly rotating and centred (x~0.45-0.55), filling about half the frame. Best seconds 4-12. The source is 1280x720 at 23.976 fps, upscaled to 1920x1080 at 30 fps. The cut begins after the on-screen caption (genus/depth text, 0-~6.5 s of the source) and the crossfade (6.6-7.4 s). No text, logos or people.
fact_en: This red jellyfish was seen during the 700-meter (2,297-foot) water column exploration in Hydrographer Canyon; scientists identified it as belonging to the genus Poralia but think it may be an undescribed species.
